title: fix: a checkbox roadmap imports into a list that already has rows
headline: A project whose improvement list is already data can now move its checkbox roadmap in, so the 1.36.0 use check has a way out. Install no longer merges a project's own state, list and decisions, and the guards close a way past them that bracketed PowerShell arguments opened.
alignment: v1.36.1 fixes what verifying 1.36.0 in the workbench found, so every kit project can finish the move to a roadmap kept as data.

items.text: `list import` of a checkbox roadmap adds its rows to a list that already holds rows, with new ids, all or nothing; a box already in the list is refused, and tables beside the boxes stay in the file.
items.where: A roadmap beside a list kept as data

items.text: Install seeds a project's state, list and decisions once and never merges, updates or folds them back, so a kit change to their templates never asks for a hand merge.
items.before: A clash to merge by hand

items.text: A folder change back after a kit script (Pop-Location, popd, after ; && or a new line) no longer makes the guards hold the script as a write to a protected file.
step move places a roadmap step before or after another, by its name or release.
A command with a bracket gets no read exemption from the guards: a PowerShell argument in brackets runs as code, and a protected path joined from pieces inside it was let through.
Import reads a heading step's spacing as one space, places its boxes at the step the state holds, and refuses two steps that differ only in spacing.

verification: Each fix has a test that fails on 1.36.0 and passes here, the sweep's fixes included.
A checkbox roadmap moves into a list that holds rows with new ids; a failed rewrite leaves the list and the state as they were, and a retry adds each box once.
An install over a project whose state, list and decisions changed leaves all three as they are, with nothing to merge.

decisions.decision: A fix release, in the same thread
decisions.why: The owner picked a 1.36.1 fix build by pop-up after the workbench verify found the dead end; 1.36.0 stays unshipped until this verifies.
The sweep showed that dropping the template hashes alone made the next upgrade clash again; the root fix is that install never merges the project's own data.

dimensions.name: Code security
dimensions.result: Bracketed arguments, folder moves back, all fixed

dimensions.name: Gaps, scaling, test value
dimensions.result: Import retries, data merges, test gaps, all fixed

fixed: The upgrade from 1.36.0 would clash on the state again; install now never merges the project's data. Fixed in 2234d6f.
A bracketed PowerShell argument could write a guard file past the read exemption. Fixed in 7e37158.
Two tests could pass with the trail and the kept marks broken. Fixed in 7e37158 and 650deb7.

upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A project the 1.36.0 use check stopped moves its checkbox roadmap with `list import` now.
limits: Boxes under a heading the state already holds as a step keep that step as it is; its carries and state are not read again.
